frameworkCheck.title: AP World History: Modern Course and Exam Description (effective Fall 2026)
frameworkCheck.how: The 71 numbered CED topics (1.1–9.9) were read from the topic pages of the current PDF on AP Central, and each is matched to the StudySprint topic whose guide section and questions teach it. A unit's final topic (comparison, causation, or continuity and change) is covered by the topic whose questions practice that reasoning. The CED's six historical thinking skills were also checked: its exam section says multiple-choice questions assess Developments and Processes, Sourcing and Situation, Claims and Evidence in Sources, Contextualization, and Making Connections, and that no multiple-choice questions explicitly assess Argumentation.
frameworkCheck.weightsSource: the AP Students course page (“On The Exam”) and the CED's unit table, both checked 2026-11-09
frameworkCheck.examFormat: From the AP Students exam page and the CED clarifications (beginning with the May 2027 exam; 3 hours 15 minutes, fully digital in Bluebook): Section IA, 55 multiple-choice questions in 55 minutes (40% of the score), in sets of usually 3–4 questions about the same source or sources (texts, images, charts, and maps); Section IB, 3 required short-answer questions in 40 minutes (20%): one with a secondary source, one with a primary source, and one with a non-text source, each on developments between 1200 and 2001; Section II, a document-based question (25%, 7 documents, 60 minutes recommended including a 15-minute reading period) and one required long essay (15%, 40 minutes) whose prompt spans about half of the course's time periods. StudySprint practice is multiple-choice only, in source-based sets; written-response practice uses College Board's released questions.
differences: The Course at a Glance titles topic 7.4 “The Economy in the Interwar Period”; the topic page prints “Economy in the Interwar Period”. StudySprint records the topic-page titles as printed.
The AP Students page's unit topic lists are summaries; the CED's 71 topics are the required content and are listed per unit as framework topics.

The CED clarifications for Fall 2026 change the short-answer and long-essay sections (all three short-answer questions are required and include sources; one long essay is required). The AP Students exam page already describes the new format.
